data.narrative:
Atomic Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis considers a peer set of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies spanning Series A through Series B, supplemented by a broader universe of eight private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $25M raised proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies a $50M valuation. Peer-median analysis across five robotics comparables—including Humanoid ($1.4B, Series A), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed)—yields a median of $1.6B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The sharp divergence between these methods reflects the stage and maturity spread within the peer sample, particularly the inclusion of later-stage, higher-valued Series B companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $42M to $1.9B, with a median of $850M. Key uncertainties driving the wide band include Atomic Industries' exact stage positioning relative to peers (Series A comps like Humanoid command substantially higher valuations), the relevance of Series B comparables for a current-stage Series A round, and product-market traction not captured in raised capital alone. A narrower range would require additional clarity on near-term funding readiness and revenue or deployment metrics.
